newsitem.title: USA: Key separatist surrenders to Texas police.
newsitem.headline: Key separatist surrenders to Texas police.

text.p: A key member of the armed Republic of Texas separatists holed up in the west Texas mountains for the past six days walked out of the group's compound on Friday and was arrested, police said.

Robert Scheidt, the security chief of the group who was returned to the compound by police earlier in exchange for the release of two hostages, was arrested without incident, Texas Department of Public Safety spokesman Mike Cox said.

"He walked out of the compound and was arrested by two DPS troopers without incident," Cox told reporters, adding that Scheidt was in police custody and would be taken to jail in the nearby town of Marfa later Friday.

Scheidt is one of six Republic of Texas members including the group's leader, Richard McLaren, who face state felony charges for engaging in criminal activity. Three of the six are also charged with aggravated kidnapping.
Police on Thursday made a "final offer" for McLaren's surrender seeking to end the standoff at the group's compound in the Davis Mountains of west Texas.
McLaren still has not responded to the offer, and Scheidt carried out a package of documents from McLaren to be delivered to McLaren's attorney Terence O'Rourke.
Police negotiators awaited word from the other 12 separatists.

Officials said they were concerned that the siege was becoming a rallying point for anti-government militias after arresting at least nine armed men in the area this week on their way to fight alongside the Republic of Texas group.
McLaren resumed communications with police on Thursday after two days of silence from his ramshackle hideout. His group says Texas is an independent nation.

Before he broke off talks, police indicated his surrender was near and the siege would end quickly and peacefully. But on Thursday, they cut off electricity to the compound he calls "the embassy" and said they had made their final offer.
"It is now in his court to respond to this," said Cox. He declined to give details of the offer and did not say how long McLaren had to respond.
McLaren's attorney Terence O'Rourke said he had advised his client "in no uncertain terms to end it."

"The (Texas) Rangers and DPS have made clear to me that the rising level of response of armed men is something that is of the utmost concern to them," he told reporters. "In some respects, this represents a somewhat more dangerous situation than Waco."
In 1993 about 80 Branch Davidian cult members were killed in a huge blaze which consumed their Texas compound at the end of a long siege by FBI agents.
"I as a lawyer for Richard McLaren and his friends have made the best deal I can: a final written offer and it is a final written offer," O'Rourke told reporters late on Thursday.

McLaren, 43, and the other Republic members have been surrounded by elite police units since Sunday when they took two hostages in retaliation for the arrest of Scheidt. The hostages were later released in an exchange for Scheidt.
On Wednesday, Texas Rangers in Peco, Texas, 70 miles (112 km) to the north, arrested seven Republic of Texas supporters travelling in two cars loaded with guns and ammunition.
Also on Wednesday, two men driving a car with Republic of Texas license plates were stopped just a few miles from the compound and arrested after police found a stolen semi-automatic rifle inside.

DPS Trooper John Barton told Reuters police got a report late on Wednesday that a caravan of three recreational vehicles and other cars carrying Republic supporters from Arkansas was within 200 miles (321 km) of Fort Davis.
"We alerted all state troopers to be on the lookout," he said, but the group, which supposedly said it was on a fishing trip to New Mexico, had not been located.
He said there were reports of other groups planning to help the Republic of Texas, but nothing confirmed. "We're asking them to stay back, stay back," Barton said.
O'Rourke said another militia member, armed with a semi-automatic rifle and a semi-automatic pistol, was arrested near the compound on Thursday.
Cox declined to say how much time McLaren had to surrender, but stressed that officials still wanted a peaceful solution to the crisis.
"We have said all along we want a peaceful outcome to this, not a Wild West outcome," said Cox.

The Republic of Texas group, formed in 1995, believes the 1845 annexation of Texas by the United States was illegal. Texas was an independent nation for nine years after breaking away from Mexico in 1836.
